title: Artin theorem for an embedded join of henselizations
statement: Let $P$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(P)$, and fix a separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ [def-kun-separably-closed]. For prime ideals $\mathfrak q_1,\mathfrak q_2\subset P$, choose $P$-embeddings $P^h_{\mathfrak q_i}\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of their ordinary henselizations [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Let $J$ be the subring of $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ generated by their images. Then $J$ is a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. If neither $\mathfrak q_1\subseteq\mathfrak q_2$ nor $\mathfrak q_2\subseteq\mathfrak q_1$, then $J$ is strictly henselian and the contraction to $P$ of its maximal ideal is strictly contained in both $\mathfrak q_i$.

source.place: Theorem 6.1, printed p. 12, citing Artin, On the joins of Hensel rings, Theorems 2.2 and 2.5. Online Huebner--Schmidt paper read; local archival copy and the original Artin paper WANTED.

proof.text: The hypotheses and notation agree with the setup of Hübner--Schmidt, Theorem 6.1: $P$ is a normal integral domain, the two primes are $\mathfrak q_1,\mathfrak q_2$, and the chosen maps are embeddings of the ordinary henselizations into the fixed separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. The subring generated by the two images is therefore their join $[P^h_{\mathfrak q_1},P^h_{\mathfrak q_2}]$. Artin's Theorem 2.2, as quoted in Theorem 6.1, says that this join is a local henselian ring. This proves the first clause.

source.place: Theorem 6.1, printed p. 12, first sentence; Artin, On the joins of Hensel rings, Theorem 2.2

proof.text: Assume neither prime contains the other. The same theorem's second clause (Artin's Theorem 2.5) applies to the identical embedded join and states that it is strictly henselian and that the pullback to $P$ of its maximal ideal is strictly contained in each of $\mathfrak q_1$ and $\mathfrak q_2$. Under the definition of strictly henselian local ring, this is exactly the remaining conclusion.
